routes.reason: Source of AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.5, the route the maintainer's guide names. NC.5 plans the depth-two quotient, the p-adic height equations, the Néron–Severi and bad-place terms and the rank-versus-genus/Picard-number criterion, and the 21 missing items sent there are exactly that theory: the quadratic Chabauty pair and the determinant criterion, nice correspondences, Nekovář's height with its local decomposition, the local height at p through mixed extensions of filtered φ-modules, A_Z(b,x), Lemma 3.7, Corollary 3.8 and the D_cris comparison. I checked the ownership claim rather than taking it: at the pinned commits neither library has a p-adic height (no declaration in Mathlib 082e2d3 or Tau Ceti f790474 matches Chabauty, Coleman, Nekovář, Néron–Severi or a p-adic height pairing), and GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.9 is the BDP setting, so nothing else owns them. The four planned items listed alongside (Theorem 2.3, nice correspondences, U_Z, Kim–Tamagawa) are named as items the paper is a good source for, which section 16 allows a source route to do. AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty has origin campaign, so the route is admissible.

Source of AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.2, added by the extraction rather than named by the guide. papers.json tells this job to 'route its items to those layers and to other existing roadmaps', so adding a companion layer in the same roadmap is what was asked, not a re-route. The fit is right: NC.2 constructs the unipotent étale and de Rham fundamental groups through their Tannakian categories with path torsors carrying filtration and Frobenius, and the 14 missing items are that machinery — Appendix A's universal pointed n-unipotent objects and path torsors, Kim's universal connection (Theorem 4.2, Lemma 4.3, Corollary 4.4), Hadian's Theorem 4.5, unipotent isocrystals and Lemma 5.2, and the Chiarellotto–Le Stum comparison. None of it is in the libraries at the pins: Mathlib's WittVector.Isocrystal is the Dieudonné-module notion over a perfect field, not an overconvergent isocrystal on a rigid space, and neither library has anything Tannakian beyond Tau Ceti's reconstruction for affine group schemes.

Source of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6, the second route the guide names. ED.6 consumes NC.5 and owns certified worked examples with termination and precision certificates, and the 28 missing items are the algorithm (the explicit connection and gauge transformations, Lemma 4.10, Theorem 4.11, the Frobenius structure (45), the splittings, Lemmas 5.5 and 5.7, precision) together with the whole X_s(13) computation and the three main theorems with their cited inputs. I reproduced the computational part of this route's subject matter independently: the two plane models of §6.3 agree under the stated substitution (the first model pulled back is Q/16), the seven listed points lie on Q, Q is smooth modulo 3, 5, 7, 11, 17, 19 and 23 and singular modulo 2 and 13, the first model is singular only modulo 13, and #X(F_17) = 20 as the extraction's gap note claims.

Source of ModularCurvesPartII:R13.5 for the six items on semi-stable models. R13.5 is 'bad fibres and regular/semistable models' and owns local models, supersingular intersections, Igusa components and the base extension needed for a semi-stable model, with its cases kept as an explicit finite list; X_0(ℓ²) over Q_ℓ^nr(ϖ) and its quotient by w_{ℓ²} add cases to that list rather than a new direction, so a source route is right and a Part II would be wrong. The layer's own list is phrased around the cases the Serre weight-and-level argument invokes, so this route widens the list; that is a matter for the roadmap's blueprint, not a reason to reject, and nothing else in the atlas computes models of X_0(ℓ²) at ℓ. ModularCurvesPartII has origin campaign. Corollary 6.7 is what makes NC.5's bad-place local heights vanish for this curve, so the route also records a real dependency between the two roadmaps.

notes: Accept. 92 items over §§1–6 and the appendix, 1 library, 22 planned and 69 missing, every missing item routed exactly once and six planned items named as sources, which section 16 permits. I reproduced both hashes the source block records — the Annals PDF e1aa5f96… and arXiv v1 77c57b03… — and read the arXiv v1 LaTeX e-print and the authors' 2023 sequel in addition. Every one of the 51 named results a locator cites is on the printed page the locator gives, and all eleven arXiv-v1 renumbering claims are right, each checked against the arXiv statement itself (Lemma 2.3, Theorem 4.1, Theorem 4.4, Lemma 4.5, Lemmas 5.3–5.5, Theorems 6.6–6.7, Corollary 6.8, Proposition 6.3). All 19 distinct planned layer ids exist in the atlas, and the library item's declarations exist at Tau Ceti f790474 and say what is claimed. The eight sourceIssues are all confirmed at their locators in the published text, with two corrections made in place: E3's quotation of the printed matrix had both integrals in the (3,1) entry as ∫_x^{x_0}, where the paper prints the iterated ω^T Zω term as ∫_{x_0}^x — checked from the glyph positions in the PDF — so that entry is inconsistent with itself and the correction now says so; and E5 gains the note that arXiv v1's Lemma 4.5 concludes in Pic(X × X) ⊗ Q_p, which the published Lemma 4.7 drops. Item 81 gains the declaration that carries its Γ_0(169) reading. E2's and E3's claims about the authors' Magma code were checked in the repository: hodge.m solves Σ_j η_j Res_x(ω_{2g+j}) = −Res_x(ω^T Z Ω), which is (30) in the paper's sign convention and not the printed step (i), and U1.m transports from the Teichmüller point to the point, the orientation of (41) and not the one printed in §5.3.2. Nothing was rejected and no item was deleted. The §6 Magma computations were not re-run and the cited theorems were read only as the paper states them; both boundaries are already recorded as gaps.
